page: Microsoft Azure D16plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Dpldsv6 server family. It is powered by a Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, featuring 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs with a dedicated 1.0 thread-per-core allocation. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 945 GB NVMe SSD and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark evaluations position this server in the average to strong performance tiers. It demonstrates strong memory bandwidth, with read-only large block speeds reaching 307.54 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 124.58 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 25% of tested hardware. Single-threaded gzip compression is also strong at 33.08 GB/sec. Other compute metrics, such as the Geekbench single-core score of 1688.0 and multi-core score of 14736.0, fall within the average range. Redis SET operations average 32.07 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reaches 27.37 GB/sec.

Due to its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server is classified as a low-memory configuration, making it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data processing. This limitation is reflected in LLM inference benchmarks, where prompt processing for a medium 7B model drops to a weak 24.62 tokens/sec. However, the combination of dedicated ARM cores, high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, and strong memory bandwidth makes it a cost-efficient choice for compute-bound workloads, web serving, application hosting, and lightweight database operations that do not require massive memory footprints.
description: The Microsoft Azure D16plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine powered by a 16-core Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. It features a dedicated CPU allocation with 16 vCPUs, 32.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 945 GB NVMe SSD. Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance delivers a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, positioning it as a compute-focused, low-memory option. Benchmark data shows strong performance in memory bandwidth, with large-block read speeds of 307.54 GB/sec, and strong single-threaded gzip compression at 33.08 GB/sec. Conversely, CPU and multi-threaded decompression benchmarks remain in the average range, and LLM inference for larger models is limited. This server is best suited for web serving, application hosting, and compute-bound tasks that benefit from dedicated ARM architecture and fast local NVMe storage without requiring high memory capacity.
